audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 row gave the stage to Teemo while whys[4], spikes[1] and mid all call level 6 your one kill window.
audit.why: packet.levelChart puts Illaoi at level 6 and Teemo everywhere else. whys[4]: 'Level-6 R gives you one kill window to hard-engage before he blinds and runs'; spikes[1]: 'Landing this is your one real kill window in an otherwise losing lane'; mid: 'your level-6 R gives one real kill window'. Leap of Faith at 120s rank 1 against a champion with no dash is the only stage Illaoi owns, and the chart was hiding it.
audit.corrected: Row 4 flipped to Illaoi in both layers with the rating raised. Every other row already reads Teemo or Skill and stays.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says in five places that Blinding Dart shuts off Harsh Lesson and the tentacle slams — spikes[0] 'disables your auto-attacks and Harsh Lesson's on-hit slam window', whys[2] 'his blind shuts off your W-slam', early 'shuts off your autos and Harsh Lesson slam', wants.foe[0] 'disable your autos and tentacle-slam windows', late 'his blind neuters your basic-attack-reliant tentacle procs'.
audit.why: Riot on Blinding Dart (Q, 7s flat, 680 range): it damages and blinds. A blind removes basic-attack damage. Harsh Lesson is an ability — a 400-range leap that deals its own physical damage and 'causes nearby Tentacles to also swing at the target' — and Tentacle Smash and Test of Spirit are abilities too. The already-audited mirror states this from the other side in as many words: 'Blinding Dart removes her auto damage but not Harsh Lesson.' The two pages currently tell opposite stories about the single most important interaction in the matchup, and this side's version tells a player their entire pattern is disabled when it is not.
audit.corrected: All five rewritten: the blind strips auto damage, the leap and its tentacle swings still land.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' and no ability on the page carries a number.
audit.why: Blinding Dart is 7s flat at every rank, Move Quick 14s flat, Toxic Shot is a permanent on-hit with no cooldown, Noxious Trap effectively 0.25s off a charge system. Against Harsh Lesson at 4s, the 7-second blind is the whole rhythm of the lane: you get two leaps per blind, and neither of them is blinded.
audit.corrected: The 7s and 14s written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and report[5], with the explicit ordering.

audit.why: The suspectNames hit on 'Harsh Lesson's' in spikes[0] is a false positive — Harsh Lesson is Riot's real name for Illaoi's W. The sentence was rewritten for the blind error, not the name.
